subject: Renewal proposal: term offset, staged ramp, and capacity top-up
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal proposal: term offset, staged ramp, and capacity top-up

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our run-through, I put together an initial amendment and two options for how DataScale could transition to a longer-term commitment while preserving the burst capacity you rely on. Key highlights: 

- Option A (36 months): staggered ramp (Year1 30% committed capacity / Year2 60% / Year3 100%), 8% volume discount vs current list, monthly metering with quarterly true-up, and a 25% burst buffer (charged only on use).
- Option B (24 months): faster ramp to full capacity (Year1 60% / Year2 100%), 5% discount, annual billing with pro-rated onboarding credit.
- Co-term: we can co-term this amendment with your existing DS-analytics seat license so all infra billing lines align on the same renewal date.
- Auto-renew: we can include a 90-day opt-out window prior to renewal. If you prefer no auto-renew, we can mark it manual and add a small uplift to pricing.

Attached is the draft amendment (Redwood_AMEND_3yr_term_v1.pdf) and our ramp playbook for how we operationalize staged capacity (redwood_ramp_playbook_v2.pdf). For procurement, we typically accept a PO referencing the amended SOW; I added a sample PO template (DataScale_REQ_PO.pdf) in case it helps.

Two asks from you to speed this along: 1) Which option do you want pricing for (A or B)? 2) Will procurement require co-terming with the DS-analytics contract or prefer a standalone amendment?

Happy to jump on a quick call later this week to walk legal and procurement through the proration and billing cadence.

Best,
Naomi

Subject: Internal: DS negotiation talking points and alternative language

Naomi / Mateo —

Drafted some negotiation language and a fallback structure to keep procurement comfortable while protecting Redwood's unit economics. Key internal points to use on the call: 

- Proration approach: initial invoice = pro-rated committed amount for the partial first billing period + one month of burst buffer as a refundable credit against the first true-up. This creates a clean PO line ("Amendment initial pro-rated committed fee") and resolves sticky accounting asks.

- Auto-renew language (proposed): "This Agreement will renew for consecutive terms equal to the initial term unless Customer provides written notice of non-renewal at least 90 days prior to the end of the then-current term." If procurement insists on opt-in, offer: "No auto-renew; renewal requires mutual execution of amendment or PO; renewal pricing subject to then-current Redwood list rates." Use the opt-in only if DataScale explicitly asks — otherwise keep the 90-day notice (industry standard).

- Safety net: add a ramp protection clause: if committed usage is missed by >25% for two consecutive quarters, Redwood will provide a one-time credit up to 10% of the quarterly committed spend to accelerate usage-to-commit conversion. This keeps them safe while preserving our retention economics.

- Pricing options: produce a final redline with exact per-token/embedding bands. I recommend pushing for Option A with 8% discount — better LTV and predictable throughput.

I've attached the redlined playbook and the language snippets (redwood_ramp_playbook_v2.pdf). If you want, I can join the Thursday procurement call to run through it.

—Camila

Elena —

Appreciate the quick review. To answer your procurement questions inline: 

1) Proration and billing: initial invoice will contain: (a) pro-rated committed fee for the remainder of the billing cycle, (b) initial refundable burst credit (1 month of burst buffer), and (c) setup/onboarding fee if you select annual billing. Quarterly true-ups will reconcile committed vs actual; any overage is billed as separate line items with thresholds and alerts. We will provide an invoice sample before PO submission.

2) Auto-renew: we can include the explicit opt-in language you requested, but note that opt-in typically results in shorter terms and slightly higher pricing. I've attached an updated amendment draft that includes both variants (one with 90-day opt-out and one explicit opt-in clause). Please review and mark which you prefer.

3) Burst charges: separate invoice line, capped at agreed monthly threshold, and we will configure two alert levels (70% and 95% of the burst cap).

Attached: Redwood_AMEND_3yr_term_v1.pdf (updated with alternate auto-renew language) and DS_Q1_usage_summary.csv (your usage detail we pulled to illustrate ramping).

Next steps: if procurement confirms co-term preference and provides a PO reference, we can prepare a DocuSign packet and route it to your legal for signature. Camila / Mateo — happy to loop you into the procurement call Thursday at 10:00 AM PT if you can make it.

Best,
Naomi
